hypothesis: Funding on two venues for the same coin differs because their rate formulas and trader bases differ (Hyperliquid adds a fixed ~11%/yr interest leg; dYdX v4 has its own). Shorting the perp on the richer venue and longing it on the cheaper one is delta-neutral with no spot leg and collects the spread. Rule: per coin, each week, trailing funding spread s = HL - dYdX (annualized, through yesterday); hold short-rich/long-cheap when |s| on capital (|s| x L/2, since both legs post 1/L margin) beats the T-bill yield, else T-bills. Universe: the point-in-time Hyperliquid top 20 intersected with dYdX markets (k-prefixed HL tickers mapped to their dYdX names). Costs: 8bp per leg per trade, daily margin top-up on both legs, liquidation of either leg when the day's high (short leg) or low (long leg) moves 1/L - 3% from the prior close, 5% penalty base with 2% and 10% sensitivities. Sample starts 2024-01-01 to skip dYdX v4's launch period of zero rates. Variants: leverage {2x, 3x} x lookback {7, 30}. PRIMARY, named now: 2x, 30 days. Pass for a defensible out-of-sample 1.5, as with strategy 21: Sharpe after 5% liquidations >= 1.5, PSR(SR>0) >= 0.95, and also >= 1.5 in 2025-26 alone since decay killed the single-venue carry. Also reported: how much of the spread is Hyperliquid's interest constant.
name: crypto cross-venue funding dispersion (Hyperliquid vs dYdX v4)
